+//! The tool stack's true z span along a move, for the fixture laws
+//! (c2) and (d2) (#424, #425). A band of the stack (flute, shank,
+//! holder, the spindle housing) rides the tip: over a move it sweeps
+//! every z from its window at the low end to its window at the high
+//! end. Law (c2) used to stand every band at the move's deepest z, so
+//! on a ramp or a plunge the top of the stack at the high end went
+//! unjudged (#425); law (d2) swept only the flute disc along an
+//! upright rapid, so the shank, holder and housing were never judged
+//! on a rapid at all (#424).
+//!
+//! The window here, per straight piece of the tip path, is
+//! `[min(floor, piece low) + lo, piece high + hi]`: the band's extent
+//! at both ends, min to max, on the piece's own z (an arc's chords,
+//! each at its own height - [`Move::segments3`]). `floor` is the
+//! law's historical bottom (the move's lower end for (c2)), so the
+//! window only ever GROWS over the one the law always read: every old
+//! verdict stands, a level move's window is the old one sum for sum,
+//! and the new hits are steel the stack really reaches at the high end.
+//! An enclosing window over-reports a graze on a long ramp, never hides
+//! a crash - the bands law's own precedent.
+//!
+//! The z test stays [`crate::fixture::band_hits_box`]'s: overlap must
+//! be strict beyond tolerance. So the strict-dip silences hold for the
+//! whole stack - a retract off a mounting face (the tip leaving
+//! exactly the box top) keeps every band at or above the steel, and
+//! flush contact is not a crash.
+//!
+//! Provenance: the swept volume of a coaxial cylinder carried along a
+//! straight segment, enclosed by its end windows - elementary solid
+//! geometry; the band/box predicate is the crate's own
+//! (`crate::fixture`). Our own design; no vendor source consulted.
+
+use crate::cl::Move;
+use crate::fixture::{band_hits_box, FixtureBox};
+use crate::tools::ToolGeom;
+use camcraft_tools::holder_profile::HolderStack;
+
+use super::types::FixturePart;
+
+/// One straight piece of a move's tip path: its XY ends and the z the
+/// tip spans over it, already floored by the law's historical bottom.
+/// A non-finite z fails closed (the window is NaN, which the band
+/// predicate reads as a hit).
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
+pub(super) struct Piece {
+    ax: f64,
+    ay: f64,
+    bx: f64,
+    by: f64,
+    z_lo: f64,
+    z_hi: f64,
+}
+
+/// The move's tip path as pieces: itself for a straight move, its 3-D
+/// chords for an arc (the same XY as [`Move::chords`]), each spanning
+/// `[min(floor, its low end), its high end]` in z.
+pub(super) fn pieces(m: &Move, chord_tol: f64, floor: f64) -> Vec<Piece> {
+    m.segments3(chord_tol)
+        .into_iter()
+        .map(|(p, q)| {
+            let finite = p.z.is_finite() && q.z.is_finite() && floor.is_finite();
+            Piece {
+                ax: p.x,
+                ay: p.y,
+                bx: q.x,
+                by: q.y,
+                z_lo: if finite { floor.min(p.z).min(q.z) } else { f64::NAN },
+                z_hi: if finite { p.z.max(q.z) } else { f64::NAN },
+            }
+        })
+        .collect()
+}
+
+/// Does the band `above..above + len` (radius `r`) strike any box
+/// anywhere along the pieces? `lean` (a non-vertical axis) turns the
+/// band's column into the leaning enclosure of law (c2): shifted to the
+/// band's mid-height point on the axis, widened by the half-length's
+/// spread, its z planes the axis reach at both window ends plus the
+/// disc's radius. Upright, the window is the bare z span. A level
+/// piece reproduces the law's historical sums exactly.
+pub(super) fn band_struck(
+    pieces: &[Piece],
+    lean: Option<[f64; 3]>,
+    above: f64,
+    r: f64,
+    len: f64,
+    fixtures: &[FixtureBox],
+) -> bool {
+    fixtures.iter().any(|b| {
+        pieces.iter().any(|pc| {
+            let (offx, offy, r_use, bz0, bz1) = match lean {
+                None => (0.0, 0.0, r, pc.z_lo + above, pc.z_hi + above + len),
+                Some(a) => {
+                    let mid = above + len * 0.5;
+                    let spread = (len * 0.5) * (a[0] * a[0] + a[1] * a[1]).sqrt();
+                    let (za0, za1) = (pc.z_lo + above * a[2], pc.z_hi + above * a[2]);
+                    let (zb0, zb1) = (pc.z_lo + (above + len) * a[2], pc.z_hi + (above + len) * a[2]);
+                    (
+                        mid * a[0],
+                        mid * a[1],
+                        r + spread,
+                        za0.min(za1).min(zb0.min(zb1)) - r,
+                        za0.max(za1).max(zb0.max(zb1)) + r,
+                    )
+                }
+            };
+            band_hits_box(
+                pc.ax + offx,
+                pc.ay + offy,
+                pc.bx + offx,
+                pc.by + offy,
+                bz0,
+                bz1,
+                r_use,
+                b,
+            )
+        })
+    })
+}
+
+/// The bands above the flute, worst first: shank, the holder cylinder,
+/// then the spindle housing (radius, length) when the machine states
+/// it, riding on the holder's top - each `(part, above, r, len)`, the
+/// shape law (c2) builds. A modelled holder body (#368's `HolderStack`)
+/// replaces the one holder cylinder here exactly as it does in (c2).
+pub(super) fn upper_bands(
+    tool: &ToolGeom,
+    holder: &HolderStack,
+    spindle: Option<(f64, f64)>,
+) -> Vec<(FixturePart, f64, f64, f64)> {
+    let mut out = vec![(FixturePart::Shank, tool.flute_len, tool.shank_radius, tool.shank_len)];
+    out.extend(holder.bands.iter().map(|b| (FixturePart::Holder, b.above, b.r, b.len)));
+    if let Some((sr, sl)) = spindle {
+        out.push((FixturePart::Spindle, holder.top, sr, sl));
+    }
+    out
+}
+
+/// Law (d2)'s whole-stack reading of an UPRIGHT rapid (#424), after
+/// its flute disc came back clear: the upper bands (`bands`, worst
+/// first, named when struck), then the flute column above the tip
+/// (reported as [`FixturePart::Rapid`], the tool body on a rapid) -
+/// each over the rapid's true z span. Band-free tools and bands of no
+/// length are no steel.
+pub(super) fn upright_rapid_struck(
+    m: &Move,
+    tool: &ToolGeom,
+    bands: &[(FixturePart, f64, f64, f64)],
+    fixtures: &[FixtureBox],
+) -> Option<FixturePart> {
+    let pcs = pieces(m, 0.01, m.from.z.min(m.to.z));
+    let upper = bands.iter().copied();
+    let flute = std::iter::once((FixturePart::Rapid, 0.0, tool.radius, tool.flute_len));
+    upper
+        .chain(flute)
+        .filter(|&(_, _, _, len)| len > 0.0 || len.is_nan())
+        .find(|&(_, above, r, len)| band_struck(&pcs, None, above, r, len, fixtures))
+        .map(|(part, ..)| part)
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+## #424, #425 - the fixture laws read the whole stack over its true z span
+
+- **Chosen:** A new module, `sim::verify::stack_span`, gives both fixture
+  laws one reading of "where the stack is along a move". Each straight
+  piece of the tip path (a straight move, or an arc's 3-D chords from
+  `Move::segments3`) gets a z span `[min(floor, piece low), piece high]`.
+  A band `above..above + len` is then judged over the window
+  `[z_lo + above, z_hi + above + len]`. That is the band's window at both
+  ends of the piece, from min to max, swept along the piece's XY with the
+  existing `fixture::band_hits_box`.
+  - **Law (c2), `bands_vs_fixtures` (#425):** every band (shank, holder,
+    spindle housing, flute column) is judged over that window, floored at
+    the move's deepest end. A ramp's high end lifts the whole stack with
+    it. The #425 repro (ramp z 0 to 40, arm at z 100..120 over the high
+    end, holder top 130 there) now reports `FixtureHit (Holder)`. The
+    leaning enclosure takes the same span: its z planes are the axis
+    reach at both window ends.
+  - **Law (d2), `rapids_vs_fixtures*` (#424):** an upright rapid keeps its
+    flute-disc test first, with the same verdict and the same `Rapid`
+    label. If the disc is clear, the shank, holder and spindle housing
+    (when the `.mch` states it) are judged over the rapid's span and
+    named when struck, then the flute column above the tip (reported as
+    `Rapid`, the tool body on a rapid). The issue's vertical retract
+    beside a bolt reports `Holder`. A low traverse past a tall bolt
+    reports `Shank` (or `Spindle` for a column only the housing reaches).
+- **Why an enclosing window, floored at the old bottom:** the window only
+  ever grows over the one each law always read. A level move's window
+  is the old one, computed with the same sums, so every existing verdict
+  stands. Every new hit is steel the stack reaches somewhere along the
+  move's span. On a long ramp the enclosure can report a graze that the
+  real sheared sweep would clear. It can never hide a crash, the same
+  trade the bands law's lean enclosure already makes.
+- **Strict-dip silences kept:** the z test is still `band_hits_box`'s
+  strict overlap. Every band stands at or above the tip, so a retract
+  off a mounting face keeps the whole stack at or above the steel and
+  stays silent. A plunge landing on a face, a traverse riding it, and a
+  band floored exactly on a box top are flush contact, also silent.
+  Penetration by a thousandth reports. All of these are pinned in
+  `sim/tests/fixture_stack_span.rs`.
+- **Non-finite z fails closed:** a piece with a non-finite z (or floor)
+  gets a NaN window, which `band_hits_box` reads as a hit. The old
+  `min`/`max` on `from.z`/`to.z` dropped a NaN silently.
+- **Considered and dropped:**
+  - *An exact sheared sweep* (the window at parameter t riding z(t), a
+    linear feasibility test inside the XY slab interval). It is tighter
+    on ramps, but it drops some hits the old pinned window reported (a
+    box low under a ramp's high end). Those verdicts would change, and
+    the issue asked that existing verdicts stand. The mesh law (#339
+    slice 1, PR #430) already sweeps the real sheared band when it judges
+    a meshed fixture, so the tighter reading arrives there.
+  - *Relabelling every upright-rapid hit by band*, the disc included.
+    The disc's `Rapid` label is a persisted verdict (cached warnings,
+    golden wording), so it stays. Only the newly judged upper bands are
+    named.
+  - *Putting the logic inline in `laws.rs`*: that file was at 380 lines.
+    The shared helper keeps it at 335, and both laws read one span rule.
+- **Cost to change later:** the window rule lives in `stack_span::pieces`
+  and `band_struck`. Tightening it to the sheared sweep is local, but it
+  needs a pass over the fixture suites for the over-reports it would
+  drop.
+- **Merging with #381 (HolderStack) and #430 (mesh):** law signatures are
+  unchanged. #381 builds c2's bands from `HolderStack` and the loop body
+  here calls `band_struck` per band, so that composes as is. The d2 upper
+  bands come from `stack_span::upper_bands(tool, spindle)`, which reads
+  the holder cylinder. When #381 lands, that helper must take the
+  `HolderStack` (shank, `holder.bands`, spindle at `holder.top`) so that
+  upright rapids judge a modelled body. Nothing will fail to compile if
+  this is missed: it has to be done by hand. #430 wraps the box laws and
+  only acquits. Its rapid mesh reading labels a convicted move `Rapid`,
+  so on a meshed fixture an upright-rapid holder hit reads `Rapid`
+  rather than `Holder`. That is a label difference only, and the post is
+  blocked either way.
